mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward 20-day returns; lower rates compress discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 3.5%, restrictive monetary policy increases discount rates for equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) and restrictive monetary policy (FEDFUNDS > 3.5%) compresses equity valuations through increased discount rates and reduced growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions characterized by strong GDP growth (GDPC1 growth > 2%) and robust labor market conditions (PAYEMS growth > 0.5%), the S&P 500 produces negative forward 5-day returns due to overvaluation and increased risk of policy tightening.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 growth > 2% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that may trigger aggressive monetary policy, producing negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The unemployment rate (UNRATE) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward 5-day returns; low unemployment rates (below 4.0%, current level 3.8%) support strong corporate earnings and positive returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE is below 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of high housing starts (HOUST > 1200) and strong retail sales (RSAFS > 500000) indicates an overheating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to increased risk of policy tightening.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are not significantly negative when HOUST > 1200 and RSAFS > 500000 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In early economic recoveries characterized by strong manufacturing output (INDPRO growth > 1.0%), the S&P 500 produces positive forward 60-day returns due to improving corporate earnings and reduced recession risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO growth > 1.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
